cards.claim: The paper introduces GameHorizon Suite, a unified data and evaluation framework designed to measure AI gameplay capabilities across multiple temporal horizons.
cards.evidence_quote: To address these challenges, as presented in Fig. 1, we introduce GameHorizon, a data and evaluation suite spanning multiple temporal horizons and AAA games.

cards.claim: Existing game datasets suffer from narrow game coverage, lacking comprehensive annotations for instructions and goals.
cards.evidence_quote: First, constrained by annotation cost, their game coverage is narrow. For instance, GameWorld (Ouyang et al., 2026) targets simple mini-games.

cards.claim: Prior evaluation methods rely on small sample sizes and online rollouts that are sensitive to specific environments and difficult to reproduce.
cards.evidence_quote: Such small samples lead to low-confidence comparisons. Online results are sensitive to specific game environments and agent harnesses, making them difficult to reproduce.

cards.claim: The GameHorizon-Annotator component automatically generates a pyramid of natural-language instructions at three temporal horizons from gameplay data.
cards.evidence_quote: GameHorizon-Annotator automatically produces a pyramid of natural-language instructions at three temporal horizons, including short-horizon operations, medium-horizon goals, and long-horizon strategies.

cards.claim: The paper introduces the GameHorizon suite, a data and evaluation framework featuring multiple temporal horizons and AAA games.
cards.evidence_quote: We introduce GameHorizon, a data and evaluation suite with multiple temporal horizons and AAA games.

cards.claim: The authors developed the GameHorizon-Annotator, a scalable pipeline designed for annotating multi-horizon instructions in gameplay.
cards.evidence_quote: GameHorizon-Annotator works as a scalable annotation pipeline for multi-horizon instructions in gameplay.

cards.claim: The GameHorizon-Data dataset contains large-scale gameplay triplets consisting of aligned videos, actions, and instructions.
cards.evidence_quote: GameHorizon-Data is a large-scale gameplay dataset with aligned triplets of videos, actions, and instructions.

cards.claim: The GameHorizon-Bench provides unified offline and stepwise online evaluations for diverse model families.
cards.evidence_quote: GameHorizon-Bench unifies reproducible offline and stepwise online evaluations for diverse model families.

cards.claim: Prior gameplay datasets suffer from narrow game coverage, limited instruction annotations, and high-variance evaluations.
cards.evidence_quote: Prior gameplay data and benchmarks suffer from narrow game coverage, limited instruction annotations, and high-variance evaluations.

cards.claim: Existing corpora lack comprehensive text instruction annotations critical for human-agent interaction.
cards.evidence_quote: Second, existing corpora lack comprehensive text instruction annotations, which are critical for human–agent interaction, e.g., instruction following and goal planning.

cards.claim: Previous benchmarks use online evaluations with limited rollouts, leading to low-confidence comparisons and poor reproducibility.
cards.evidence_quote: Such small sample sizes lead to low-confidence comparisons. Online results are sensitive to game environments and custom harnesses, making them difficult to reproduce.

cards.claim: GameHorizon provides a unified data and evaluation suite featuring 5,000 hours of recordings, diverse AAA game genres, and reproducible benchmarks.
cards.evidence_quote: In contrast, GameHorizon provides a unified data and evaluation suite, featuring 5,000 hours of recordings, diverse AAA game genres, multi-horizon instructions, and reproducible offline-online benchmarks.

cards.claim: GameHorizon-Data is a large-scale dataset containing 4,571 videos and over 6 million instructions covering 21 game titles.
cards.evidence_quote: In total, GameHorizon-Data contains 4,571 videos recorded at 60 fps and 411.03 million keyboard-mouse action events. It is annotated with 6,184,036 distinct instructions... It covers 5,000 hours of human gameplay from 21 game titles

cards.claim: The GameHorizon-Annotator pipeline produces a three-level pyramid of instructions ranging from short-horizon operations to long-horizon strategies.
cards.evidence_quote: To this end, our GameHorizon-Annotator produces a three-level pyramid of instructions, including short-horizon operations (1–5 seconds), medium-horizon goals (1–2 minutes), and long-horizon strategies (5–8 minutes).

cards.claim: GameHorizon-Data provides substantially denser annotations than prior work, with one short-horizon instruction every 2.63 seconds on average.
cards.evidence_quote: On average, GameHorizon-Data provides one distinct short-horizon instruction every 2.63 seconds... Our annotations are substantially denser than those in prior work. For example, Open-P2P (Yue et al., 2026) includes only one instruction every few minutes

cards.claim: GameHorizon-Bench features reproducible offline and stepwise online testing to evaluate model families across diverse tasks.
cards.evidence_quote: Finally, leveraging GameHorizon-Data, we introduce GameHorizon-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark featuring reproducible offline and stepwise online testing across diverse model families.

cards.claim: The GameHorizon-Annotator constructs a three-level instruction pyramid consisting of short-horizon operations, medium-horizon goals, and long-horizon strategies.
cards.evidence_quote: GameHorizon-Annotator constructs a three-level instruction pyramid, i.e., short-horizon operations, medium-horizon goals, and long-horizon strategies.

cards.claim: The system uses action-aware segmentation based on keyboard-mouse traces to identify key action transitions and determine clip boundaries.
cards.evidence_quote: To address this issue, we perform action-aware segmentation using keyboard-mouse traces to identify key action transitions and determine clip boundaries.

cards.claim: A dynamic programming algorithm enforces level-specific duration ranges of 1–5 seconds for L1, 1–2 minutes for L2, and 5–8 minutes for L3.
cards.evidence_quote: Besides, we apply a dynamic programming algorithm (Bellman, 1966) to enforce level-specific duration ranges of 1–5 seconds for L1, 1–2 minutes for L2, and 5–8 minutes for L3.

cards.claim: The VLM disambiguates action semantics by examining video frames to refine initial segmentation into short-horizon clips.
cards.evidence_quote: we employ a VLM (Google DeepMind, 2026a) to examine video frames, disambiguate action semantics, and refine the initial segmentation to a final set of short-horizon clips.

cards.claim: The GameHorizon-Data corpus comprises 5,000 hours of human gameplay across 21 game titles.
cards.evidence_quote: the corpus comprises 5,000 hours of human gameplay across 21 game titles

cards.claim: GameHorizon-Data is the first dataset to feature large-scale data, AAA focus, direct human actions, instruction annotations, dense instructions, and multi-horizon capabilities.
cards.evidence_quote: GameHorizon-Data (Ours) ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ AAA; human actions; dense multi-horizon instructions.

cards.claim: The dataset contains 411.03 million keyboard-mouse action events and over 6 million textual instructions across three horizons.
cards.evidence_quote: GameHorizon-Data contains 411.03 million keyboard-mouse action events... The retained footage is annotated with 6,184,036 textual instructions

cards.claim: The average instruction span increases across horizons, from 2.63 seconds for L1 to 330.4 seconds for L3.
cards.evidence_quote: the average duration increases across horizons, i.e., 2.63 seconds for L1, 82.6 seconds for L2, and 330.4 seconds for L3.

cards.claim: GameHorizon-Data is the first dataset to jointly provide large-scale AAA gameplay, direct human actions, and dense multi-horizon instructions.
cards.evidence_quote: Our dataset is the first corpus that jointly provides large-scale AAA gameplay, direct human actions, and dense multi-horizon instructions.

cards.claim: Unlike most datasets restricted to single games, GameHorizon-Data contains 5,000 hours of gameplay across 21 titles with a primary focus on AAA games.
cards.evidence_quote: In contrast, GameHorizon-Data contains 5,000 hours of gameplay across 21 titles, with a primary focus on AAA games.

cards.claim: GameHorizon-Bench is a unified benchmark that evaluates multi-horizon gameplay capabilities through reproducible offline and stepwise online tracks.
cards.evidence_quote: Leveraging our data, we develop GameHorizon-Bench, a unified benchmark that evaluates multi-horizon gameplay capabilities across diverse model families through the reproducible offline and stepwise online tracks.

cards.claim: The single-horizon action task (T1) asks models to make correct action decisions based on input frames and short-horizon instructions.
cards.evidence_quote: To be specific, as shown in Fig. 4, the single-horizon action task (T1) asks models to make the correct action decision based on input frames and the short-horizon instruction (L1).

cards.claim: The GameHorizon Suite evaluates long-horizon gameplay through order-dependent causal tasks and order-flexible thematic tasks, each containing 2-6 verifiable subtasks.
cards.evidence_quote: It evaluates long-horizon gameplay through order-dependent causal tasks and order-flexible thematic tasks, each comprising 2–6 verifiable short-horizon subtasks.

cards.claim: The online track consists of 10 causal and 10 thematic tasks with 62 short-horizon subtasks implemented in Minecraft.
cards.evidence_quote: Specifically, the online track comprises 10 causal and 10 thematic tasks with 62 short-horizon subtasks. Due to the inaccessibility of underlying game states in most AAA titles, we implement the online track in Minecraft

cards.claim: GameHorizon-Bench evaluates 47 models across five types including VLMs, UMMs, GUI, coding, and game agents.
cards.evidence_quote: First, with a primary focus on AAA titles, GameHorizon-Bench evaluates 47 models on 21 games, e.g., VLMs, UMMs, GUI, coding, and game agents.

cards.claim: Unlike prior work that tests limited model types mainly on Minecraft or non-AAA games, GameHorizon-Bench focuses on AAA titles.
cards.evidence_quote: Prior work tests limited model types mainly on Minecraft (Fan et al., 2022; Zheng et al., 2025; Ju et al., 2026) or non-AAA games (Paglieri et al., 2025; Zhang et al., 2026; Ouyang et al., 2026).

cards.claim: The GameHorizon-Bench evaluation shows a mean accuracy of 64.7%, which is substantially higher than the 25% random baseline, indicating the tasks are solvable yet challenging.
cards.evidence_quote: The mean accuracy across our benchmark is 64.7%, substantially above the 25% random baseline, suggesting that the designed tasks are solvable yet challenging for meaningful evaluation.

cards.claim: The benchmark distinguishes model performance clearly, with accuracy ranging from 44.6% to 80.2% across a span of 35.6 percentage points.
cards.evidence_quote: accuracy ranges from 44.6% to 80.2%, spanning 35.6 percentage points and clearly distinguishing models in

cards.claim: The evaluation protocol uses unified multiple-choice questions for offline tasks, where models directly output selections to ensure standardized and reproducible results.
cards.evidence_quote: We adopt unified MCQs for all offline tasks. Each model receives the same four-option questions and directly outputs the selections, ensuring standardized and reproducible evaluation.

cards.claim: Dedicated game agents are evaluated on action prediction by matching sequences against options using alignment scores, with incorrect predictions marked if scores fall below a threshold.
cards.evidence_quote: Thus, we evaluate these models only on the single-horizon action task (T1) by matching their action predictions against the four options via sequence alignment

cards.claim: Proprietary models dominate the leaderboard, with GPT-6-Astra achieving the highest accuracy of 80.2%.
cards.evidence_quote: GPT-6-Astra ranks first with 80.2% overall accuracy

cards.claim: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) are less competitive in gameplay tasks, with the best model BAGEL-7B-MoT achieving only 61.4%.
cards.evidence_quote: All four models fall into Tier 3 or Tier 4, indicating that current UMMs remain less competitive in gameplay tasks... BAGEL-7B-MoT achieves 61.4%

cards.claim: Unifying understanding and generation can introduce interference, as InternVL-U-4B underperforms its backbone by 1.4 percentage points.
cards.evidence_quote: InternVL-U-4B underperforms InternVL3.5-2B by 1.4 percentage points. The result suggests that unifying understanding and generation could introduce interference

cards.claim: Dedicated game agents perform near random baseline on unseen AAA games, with JARVIS-VLA dropping to 28.1% after fine-tuning.
cards.evidence_quote: the three game agents perform near the 25% random baseline on unseen AAA games... JARVIS-VLA... achieves 54.2% on the in-domain Minecraft data... However, the accuracy drops to 28.1% on unseen AAA games.

cards.claim: Enabling thinking improves accuracy for capable models like GLM-5V-Turbo and Doubao-Seed-2.1-Pro but reduces it for lightweight models like UI-TARS-1.5-7B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
cards.evidence_quote: Enabling thinking improves the accuracy of GLM-5V-Turbo and Doubao-Seed-2.1-Pro by 5.6 and 9.3 percentage points... In contrast, thinking reduces the accuracy of UI-TARS-1.5-7B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B by 8.2 and 5.9 percentage points.

cards.claim: Models consistently perform better on current-action perception than future-action planning, with an average gap of 9.9 to 23.8 percentage points depending on input settings.
cards.evidence_quote: On average, perception outperforms planning by 9.9 percentage points with frames only, 23.8 points with short-horizon instructions, and 18.2 points with multi-horizon instructions.

cards.claim: Adding short-horizon instructions to visual inputs improves average action perception accuracy by 14.1 percentage points without fine-tuning.
cards.evidence_quote: Average accuracy increases by 14.1 percentage points, from 44.5% with frames only to 58.6% with short-horizon instructions.

cards.claim: Models perform substantially better on bottom-up abstraction (98.4%) than top-down decomposition (69.5%), showing a 28.9 percentage point gap.
cards.evidence_quote: Average accuracy reaches 98.4% for abstraction but only 69.5% for decomposition, with a gap of 28.9 percentage points.

cards.claim: Online performance rankings closely align with offline tier rankings, proving the offline track is an effective indicator of online gameplay ability.
cards.evidence_quote: Models from offline Tiers 1–4 occupy online ranks 1–3, 4–6, 7–9, and 10–12, respectively. The positive association proves that our offline track captures relevant abilities and provides an effective indicator of online gameplay performance.

cards.claim: Adding action sequences to the cross-horizon consistency task causes only modest performance degradation, with accuracy decreasing by just 0.6 percentage points.
cards.evidence_quote: Average accuracy decreases from 74.0% without actions to 73.4% with actions, corresponding to a loss of 0.6 percentage points.

cards.claim: The stepwise protocol with game resets can localize failures to specific operations, supporting fine-grained diagnosis in long-horizon gameplay.
cards.evidence_quote: The stepwise protocol with game resets can localize failures to specific operations. E.g., we can distinguish models that do not know how to craft a cake from those that understand the procedure but perform a certain step incorrectly.

cards.claim: The authors propose GameHorizon, a unified suite that measures gameplay capabilities at different horizons across diverse model families.
cards.evidence_quote: We propose GameHorizon, a unified data and evaluation suite that measures gameplay capabilities at different horizons across diverse model families.

cards.claim: GameHorizon-Annotator automatically builds a dense instruction pyramid spanning short-horizon operations, medium-horizon goals, and long-horizon strategies.
cards.evidence_quote: First, GameHorizon-Annotator can automatically build a dense instruction pyramid spanning short-horizon operations, medium-horizon goals, and long-horizon strategies.

cards.claim: The authors construct GameHorizon-Data, a large-scale AAA gameplay dataset with temporally aligned videos, actions, and multi-horizon instructions in 21 titles.
cards.evidence_quote: Second, we construct GameHorizon-Data, a large-scale AAA gameplay dataset with temporally aligned videos, actions, and multi-horizon instructions in 21 titles.

cards.claim: GameHorizon-Bench combines reproducible offline evaluation with stepwise online testing to enable standardized model comparisons and fine-grained failure diagnosis.
cards.evidence_quote: Third, based on our data, GameHorizon-Bench combines reproducible offline evaluation with stepwise online testing, enabling standardized model comparisons and fine-grained failure diagnosis.

rejected.claim: Long-horizon tasks remain difficult for current models, with GPT-6-Astra achieving the highest success rate of 45.0% while ten other models achieve at most 10.0%.
rejected.evidence_quote: GPT-6-Astra achieves the highest success rate of 45.0%, while ten of the twelve models achieve at most 10.0%. The results expose existing limitations in long-horizon game planning and strategy formulation.
